summary.text: 中 is an old pictographic graph whose early forms show a long shaft crossing a central circular or square feature, sometimes with streamers. The feature’s identity is disputed, and no secure path from the early design to the common meaning “middle; center” is established.

formation.text: Treat 中 as a pictographic whole: reported early forms show a long shaft crossing a central feature, sometimes with streamers. Proposals identify it as a flag or marker, drum, or ritual pole, but the referent remains unsettled. The reviewed analysis rejects the arrow-and-target account. The later Shuowen analysis instead parses an enclosure crossed by a vertical line; it does not establish the early design.

components.text: The early graph is described as a shaft crossing a circular or square feature, sometimes with streamers. Since the feature’s referent is disputed, this records the proposed pictorial whole rather than identified modern parts.
In the received Shuowen analysis, 口 is an enclosure in a later parsing of the graph. This interpretation is not an established breakdown of the earliest forms.
In that Shuowen analysis, 丨 is the line passing through the enclosure from top to bottom. This later interpretation does not establish the line’s role in the earliest graph.

history.text: Late Shang oracle-bone and bronze forms are reported with a long shaft and a circular or square central feature. Some have streamer strokes and others do not; Western Zhou bronze forms continue both types, and some omit the central feature. Later records include Warring States, Qin, seal-script, and Han clerical forms. The selected seal-script image is a modern redraw of a later form, not an excavated early glyph.
The received Shuowen analysis parses 中 as 口 with 丨 passing through it from top to bottom, and glosses it as “inside.” This historical account does not settle the early graph’s referent.

uncertainties.text: The identity or function of the early central feature remains unsettled. Flag or marker, drum, ritual pole, and wind-related interpretations have been proposed; these accounts differ, and none establishes one referent across the early forms.

Reported Shang contexts include 立中 and other proposed uses, but their precise lexical values depend on interpretation. The evidence does not establish that “middle” was the earliest sense or a semantic path from a particular depicted object to “middle,” “inside,” or “hit/attain.”
The character’s readings and reconstructions do not establish a phonetic component or a whole-graph sound borrowing; the inspected paleographic analyses identify neither.

senses.gloss: uses in Shang-period contexts, precise values unresolved
senses.text: The graph is reported in dated Shang divination contexts, including 立中 and passages associated with warfare, weather observation, and ancestral rites. These attest graph use, but the exact word meaning in each passage is unsettled.
中 commonly means “middle” or “center.” The evidence does not show that this was necessarily its earliest lexical meaning.
The received Shuowen gloss is “inside.” The evidence supports this as a historical dictionary interpretation, but does not independently establish it as a lexical sense or settle its chronology.

中 is reported with the meanings “hit the center” or “attain.” A departing-tone reading is associated with hitting the center, but the evidence does not establish when or how this use relates to “middle.”

limitations.text: The reported Shang examples do not fix 中’s precise meaning in context, and the evidence supplies no secure semantic bridge among those uses, “middle,” “inside,” and “hit/attain.”

Readings associated with “middle” and “hit the center” are distinguished, but their relationship could reflect semantic development, another historical process, or an older distinction; the evidence does not decide among these possibilities.

overview.text: 中 is an old picture of a shaft crossing a central feature. It commonly means “middle” or “center,” though the feature’s identity and the link between the early picture and that meaning remain uncertain.

components.text: The early graph is one picture: a shaft crosses a central feature whose identity is disputed.
A later dictionary analysis reads 口 as an enclosure, but this does not settle what the early picture showed.
In that later analysis, this is the line through the enclosure, not a confirmed part of the early picture.

relationships.text: The early graph is described as a whole pictorial form; this does not claim that it divides into separate modern components.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script style; modern digital redraw uploaded 2006, revised 2018
items.tradition: Chinese seal-script style, identified by the source as Shuowen seal script
items.caption: A modern redraw of 中 in Shuowen seal-script style: a vertical stroke passes through a rounded enclosure. This illustrates a later traditional form, not an excavated Shang glyph.
items.alt: Black seal-script form of 中, with a vertical stroke crossing a rounded enclosure, on a white background.
items.selection_reason: The image clearly shows the traditional seal-script form associated with the received Shuowen analysis, which describes 中 as 从口、丨，上下通. It helps illustrate that later account; it does not establish the referent of the early central feature.
